rationales.A1: Exclusively suffixing (0 native prefixes), agglutinative right-edge suffix chains (Stem+Deriv+Pl/Obl+Case; Krishnamurti 2003). Minor -0.05 for 5 initial-biased signs (title/honorific openers).
rationales.A2: Compact invariant agglutinative nominal suffix set (~6-8 cases + 3 gender/number markers *-an/*-al/*-ar; Krishnamurti 2003), matching 10 terminal signs covering 67% of final slots and invariant 740->090->400 stacking.
rationales.A3: Strictly Modifier-Before-Head / Head-Final NP (Num->N, Adj->N, Gen->N, SOV; Krishnamurti 2003), matching Num->Fish (254:59, 4.31x) and Num(013-019)->Core (97:36, 2.69x). -0.10 for unexplained postposed 705/706->033 (87:0).
rationales.A4: Productive lexical, distributive, and expressive reduplication (Krishnamurti 2003); non-discriminating (shared across all 4 families).
rationales.A5: High compatibility: Mature Harappan Rakhigarhi genome I6113 (Shinde et al. 2019 Cell) + Narasimhan et al. 2019 Science show zero Steppe ancestry in IVC (2600-1900 BCE); deep South Asian Dravidian presence (Brahui + Rigvedic Dravidian loans; Witzel 1999, Southworth 2005).

rationales.A1: Exclusively suffixing, agglutinative right-edge suffix stacking via Suffixaufnahme (Stolper 2004; Khacikjan 1998); matches 209:1 suffix-vs-prefix stack asymmetry.
rationales.A2: Small invariant agglutinative nominal class + case set (-k, -t, -r, -p, -me, -n, -na; ~7-10 bound markers; Stolper 2004), tightly matching Indus terminal bottleneck.
rationales.A3: MAJOR FALSIFIER: Elamite NPs are strictly Head-Initial (N->Adj, N->Num, N->Gen; Stolper 2004; Khacikjan 1998), directly contradicting corpus Num->Fish (254:59, p=2.54e-26) and Num(013-019)->Core (97:36). Partial credit only for 705/706->033 (87:0).
rationales.A4: Very productive root/stem reduplication (e.g., hut- -> huthut; Khacikjan 1998); shared feature.
rationales.A5: Moderate compatibility: Chronologically contemporary (2600-1900 BCE) and compatible with deep Iranian-plateau ancestry cline, active Susa-Meluhha trade, but geographic center lies ~1,500 km west in SW Iran.

rationales.A1: Mixed: Nominal phrases stack right-edge enclitics (=ene, =ak, =e, =ra, =a), BUT verbs carry a dense 7-slot PREFIX chain (modal+ventive+dimensional; Jagersma 2010), conflicting with 209:1 suffix-over-prefix stack dominance unless corpus is 100% verbless NPs.
rationales.A2: Compact invariant agglutinative NP clitic/case set (~10 cases + plural + possessives; Zolyomi 2017), compatible with Indus right-edge bottleneck.
rationales.A3: MAJOR FALSIFIER: Standard Sumerian NPs are strictly Head-Initial (N->Adj->Num, e.g., udu nita as; Jagersma 2010; Zolyomi 2017), contradicting Num->Fish (254:59) and Num(013-019)->Core (97:36). Partial credit for Ur III ledger Num->Commodity notation and 705/706->033.
rationales.A4: Productive plural/distributive/imperfective reduplication (kur-kur, mul-mul; Jagersma 2010); shared feature.
rationales.A5: HARD HISTORICAL FALSIFIER: Ur III cuneiform texts explicitly record official Meluhha interpreters (eme-bal me-luh-ha; Possehl 2002; Parpola 1994), proving Meluhhans (IVC) did NOT speak Sumerian despite active trade.

rationales.A1: Nominal inflection is suffixing, BUT Vedic employs productive verbal prefixes/preverbs (pra-, vi-, sam-, upa-, a-), past augment a-, and negative a-/an-, and does not stack 2-3 invariant agglutinative case suffixes (Macdonell 1910).
rationales.A2: MAJOR STRUCTURAL MISMATCH: Highly fusional nominal paradigm (8 cases x 3 numbers x 3 genders x multiple stem declensions + sandhi/ablaut = 30-50+ portmanteau endings), conflicting with one invariant suffix (740) ending 34.6% of all sequences and stacking cleanly (740->090->400).
rationales.A3: Predominantly Modifier-Before-Head (Num->N, Adj->N, SOV; Macdonell 1910), matching Num->Fish (254:59) and Num(013-019)->Core (97:36), with freer order permitting postposed measures.
rationales.A4: Productive verbal reduplication (perfect/intensive) + amredita nominal doubling; shared feature.

Proto-Dravidian.note: Attested Old Tamil aru-min ('6-star' = Pleiades), mu-m-min ('3-star' = Orion), mai-min ('black-star' = Saturn; Parpola 1994). Caveat: 017 (7)->220 elu-min occurs only 1x in strict deduplicated corpus while 032/002 (2)->220 occurs 59x.

Elamite.note: No attested native 6-star / 3-star constellation compounds (sparse corpus caveat).

Sumerian.note: Pleiades is reduplicated mul-mul (cf. 219=220+220, 7x), NOT 6-star; Orion is sipa-zi-an-na, NOT 3-star.

Vedic Sanskrit.note: Pleiades is Krttikah (NOT sat-tara); Orion is Mrgasiras (NOT tri-tara); cultural 6/7-star lore exists without numeral+fish/star lexical structure.

C2_seven_brazier_altar_017_585.corpus_anchor: 017 (7) -> 585 (Brazier/Altar, 17x, PMI +7.03; 585 enriched on Copper/Kiln tablets lift 4.2x-9.0x)

Proto-Dravidian.note: Sacred heptads exist in South Asian Dravidian folklore (elu-kanniyar), but no pre-Sanskritic DEDR compound specifically pairing '7 + fire-brazier'.

Elamite.note: Heptadic divine assemblies occur in Elamite religion, no direct 7+brazier compound attested.

Sumerian.note: Sacred heptad imin-bi ('The Seven'), 7 abgal sages, and 7 ritual braziers/censers attested in Mesopotamian ritual.

Vedic Sanskrit.note: Exact cultural compound: Agni saptajihva ('seven-tongued fire'), sapta-hotr ('7 fire-priests'), sapta-dhaman ('7 hearths'), saptarsi ('7 seers'). Likely reflects shared South Asian Bronze-Age substrate ritual (Kalibangan/Lothal fire altars).

Proto-Dravidian.note: Explains preposed Num->700 (20:8) & pottery 034/697, but postposed 705/706->033 (87:0) requires 033 to be either a postposed measure/tally or a grammatical/phonetic syllable.

Elamite.note: Head-initial N->Num fits 705/706->033 (87:0), but conflicts with Num->700 (20:8) and Num->Fish (254:59).

Sumerian.note: Fits postposed N->Num (705/706->033) and accounting tallies; conflicts with predominant Num->Noun order on seals.

Vedic Sanskrit.note: Same mixed profile as Proto-Dravidian: preposed Num->700 (20:8) fits, postposed 705/706->033 requires accounting-tally or non-numeral reading of 033.

test_c_holdout_prediction.epistemological_caveat: Test C evaluates TYPOLOGICAL generalization (agglutinative suffix-stacking + Modifier-Before-Head order), NOT unique genetic descent. Any extinct unknown language isolate sharing Proto-Dravidian's morphosyntactic typology would achieve the exact same out-of-sample masked-sign prediction gain.
